info.title: PBCP head: the human API
info.description: What the owner’s devices call: the brief, cards, decisions, orders, settings. Producers use the PBCP protocol routes instead (RFC §7), which this document does not cover; sign-in (/api/auth/*) is not in it either. Every /api/me request needs `Authorization: Session <access token>` and may carry `X-Timezone`.

post.summary: Trade a pairing code from the owner for your own producer token (public; no credential)
post.description: The code (six characters shown as two groups of three (XXX-XXX); the dash is optional when entering) is the credential: a request with an Authorization header is refused (400). A code that does not exist, has expired or was used is 400 `invalid_code`; no other code is touched. With a good code, a malformed root is 400 `invalid_root` and a taken one 409 `root_taken`, and the code stays usable. Rate-limited per address (429).

post.summary: Ask for an invite to the hosted head (public; no credential)
post.description: The front door’s form. A request with an Authorization header is refused (400). An address already asked is accepted again and changes nothing. No mail is sent. Rate-limited per address (429). A form-encoded post (the form without JavaScript) is answered 303 to `/?invite=requested`.

XTimezone.name: X-Timezone
XTimezone.description: The IANA timezone the device is in now, e.g. `Europe/Copenhagen`. Optional on every /api/me request. It is stored on the calling device, and the head follows the zone of the device most recently seen with it (for the brief and its days, snooze presets and the nightly card) unless the owner set an override in /api/me/settings. An unknown zone, or a bare offset such as `+02:00`, is 400 `invalid_request`, checked after the credential.
